title: Onboarding acceptance contract and upgrade path for third-party open models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We accept an increasing number of community/open models into the catalog, but there is ambiguity in what constitutes a passing intake for production-serving (pinning policy, compatibility metadata, and upgrade/rollback behavior). This ambiguity leads to late engineering rework, unexpected runtime regressions, and customer confusion when variants are swapped or unpinned.

Goal: Define a clear, implementable acceptance contract for new third-party/open model entries that covers required metadata, automated runtime checks, pinning semantics, upgrade path for minor/major upstream changes, and explicit rollback criteria. The deliverable is a short PRD + checklist consumed by intake, runtime, and QA teams, plus a set of machine-checkable sanity tests run during model ingestion.

Scope (in):
- New model intake flow for community/open weights (all architectures) for catalog ingestion
- Required metadata fields (compat tags, seq_len_profile, quantization_tolerance, recommended runtime profile)
- Clear pinning categories and conditional exemptions for experimental variants
- Automated runtime sanity checks: startup load, sample inference latency, KV cache correctness smoke, token-level generation regression on a fixed prompt suite
- Upgrade path and compatibility policy for minor patch releases vs major weights changes
- Rollback triggers and automated fallback routing plan

Scope (out):
- Deep performance tuning and kernel-level optimization (handled by serving runtime team tickets)
- Legal/IP provenance verification process (handled by Security/Legal intake)

Constraints & assumptions:
- Intake pipeline can run a fixed suite of tests within 60 minutes per model on the dedicated profiling cluster (ENG-5821).
- Not all models will be allowed to be automatically unpinned without a manual review if they exceed compatibility risk thresholds.
- We accept that some experimental models will be flagged "experimental" and granted a limited lifecycle.

Key trade-offs considered:
1) Strict gating (high friction for contributors) vs loose gating (faster catalog growth but more runtime risk). We propose a hybrid: automated gate for core signals, manual review for flagged deviations.
2) Always-pin-by-default vs always-unpin-by-default. We recommend "pin-by-default for GA+ stable signals, soft-pin for experimental variants" so customers get predictability while allowing rapid iteration.
3) Adding many required metadata fields increases intake accuracy but raises contributor burden. We limit required fields to a minimal safe set and make other fields recommended with good defaults.

Acceptance Criteria (machine-human mix):
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake template: every new open-model submission includes required metadata fields: model.name, model.version, upstream-vcs or provenance link, seq_len_profile (P95), tokenizer_id, expected_max_context, quantization_compatibility (int8/ql4/float16), and runtime_tag(s) (e.g., 'kv-cache-safe', 'vocab-alias-safe').

A2: Automated sanity run: the ingestion pipeline executes the profiling suite and returns a pass/fail with artifacts (profiling report, latency histograms, output diffs) within 60m for 95% of models on profiling cluster. Failure reasons must be machine-readable.

A3: Regression checks: generation on the canonical 6-prompt suite must not introduce hallucination increase >5% (measured by the curated eval) and per-token latency regression <50% versus baseline variant; otherwise the model is flagged for manual review.

A4: Pin semantics documented: 'GA' models default to pinned=stable; 'experimental' models default to pinned=soft with auto-expiry (30d) unless manually escalated. Pinning exceptions must be recorded with rationale.

A5: Upgrade policy: minor upstream weight-only changes (no tokenizer/arch change) can be linked as 'compatible' and scheduled for rolling update with canary traffic; major topology or tokenizer changes require a new catalog entry and manual migration plan.

A6: Fallback & rollback: runtime must support automatic fallback to last-known-good variant when health checks fail for a route; rollout automation must be able to escalate rollback within 5 minutes of crossing health thresholds.
A7: Documentation: catalog onboarding doc + short checklist published in Confluence and linked in intake UI; intake UI surfaces required fields and a preflight checklist.
A8: Developer flow: a GitHub PR template for catalog entries is created that mirrors required metadata and attaches automated profiling artifacts; PRs without artifacts are blocked from merge.
tasks: T1: Draft the short PRD and checklist (this ticket) and iterate with Runtime/Infra/QA (owner: PM).
T2: Implement required metadata schema in catalog ingestion JSON schema (owner: ENG, ref ENG-6012).
T3: Add the profiling suite to ingestion CI and surface artifacts on PRs (owner: ENG-QA).
T4: Define pin-by-default policy and auto-expiry rules; update Console display for pin state (owner: Product + Console UX).
T5: Create runtime canary + rollback playbook and map signals to automated thresholds (owner: Runtime).
T6: Publish Confluence page and add intake UI help text + PR template (owner: PM + Docs).
T7: Run pilot with 3 community models and capture issues/false-positives (owner: PM).

2026-03-03 - Diego Martinez (Assignee): Spoke with ENG infra; 60m looks reasonable for typical 3B-7B models on profiling cluster. ENG-5821 will add resource quotas for profiling jobs.
2026-03-05 - Ravi Kapoor (Runtime): Suggested adding KV-cache correctness smoke test (will add 3 synthetic prompts). Marked dependency ENG-6012.

2026-03-07 - Design review (Lena Chen): Console needs a clear state for 'soft-pinned (experimental)' with tooltip explaining auto-expiry. Linked figma above. UX follow-up: add small banner in catalog entry page.
2026-03-09 - Security (Marta Ruiz): Confirmed provenance link is necessary; suggested adding optional 'license' field in metadata. Not a hard blocker but recommended.
2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Implemented schema PR draft and opened ingestion PR (see links). Added machine-readable failure reasons enumerated in the CI job.
2026-03-12 - QA (Priya Singh): Ran local pilot on two community models; one failed the regression threshold due to tokenizer mismatch. Added test case to catch tokenizer drift earlier.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Incorporated feedback into acceptance criteria A2/A3/A5. Requesting sign-off from Runtime + QA so we can merge schema and enable blocking PR rule in catalog.
notes: Implementation note: aim to keep required metadata minimal and provide tooling to auto-populate common fields from upstream model cards to reduce contributor friction.

Longer-term: plan a compatibility signal registry (lightweight) that can be queried at routing time to choose safe fallbacks; this ticket only defines the intake contract and immediate rollout/rollback behavior.
